# UnlearnBench

[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Code style: ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff)
[![CI](https://github.com/soumikbhatta/unlearnbench/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/soumikbhatta/unlearnbench/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**Multi-Attack Verification for Machine Unlearning**

> *CS 590NN/690NN — Neural Networks in AI and Neuroscience · University of Massachusetts Amherst · Spring 2026*

---

## Overview

Machine unlearning is the problem of removing the influence of specific training data from a model without full retraining — motivated by regulatory requirements such as GDPR's "right to be forgotten." Existing methods are typically verified using a single signal: **Membership Inference Attack (MIA)**, which tests whether an adversary can still identify whether a data point was in the training set.

**The problem:** MIA can be defeated through confidence calibration while structural traces of forgotten data remain in model weights, activations, and the loss landscape. A model can *look* unlearned without *being* unlearned.

**UnlearnBench** addresses this with an ensemble of five verification signals applied uniformly across multiple unlearning baselines and datasets, enabling a rigorous oracle-grounded comparison.

---

## Research Question

> Can multi-signal verification expose residual data traces that single-signal MIA verification misses?

We define the **Oracle Gap** as the measurable distance between an unlearned model and a model retrained from scratch (the gold standard). A perfect unlearning method has zero Oracle Gap across all verification signals.

---

## Verification Signals

| Signal                           | Description                                                   | Tier     |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| **MIA**                          | Membership inference attack on the forget set                 | Tier 1   |
| **Oracle Gap (Weight Distance)** | L2 / cosine distance to retrained oracle parameters           | Tier 1   |
| **Activation Analysis**          | Hidden-layer response similarity on forgotten vs. unseen data | Tier 2   |
| **Feature Attribution**          | Saliency map alignment on forgotten samples (GradCAM)         | Tier 2   |
| **Loss Landscape**               | Hessian eigenspectrum trace on the forget set                 | Tier 3 ↗ |

---

## Baseline Unlearning Methods

| Method                | Type                                                        | Reference                       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **Fisher Forgetting** | Approximate — noise injection via Fisher Information Matrix | Golatkar et al., NeurIPS 2020   |
| **Gradient Ascent**   | Approximate — maximize loss on forget set                   | —                               |
| **SISA Training**     | Exact — sharded training with selective retraining          | Bourtoule et al., IEEE S&P 2021 |

---

## Datasets

| Dataset         | Tasks                                             | Difficulty   |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| **Split-MNIST** | 5 binary classification tasks (digit pairs)       | Baseline     |
| **CIFAR-10**    | 5 tasks (2 classes each)                          | Medium       |
| **CelebA**      | Attribute-level forgetting (40 binary attributes) | Stretch goal |

---

## Repository Layout

```
unlearnbench/
├── src/unlearnbench/          # Core library
│   ├── datasets/              # Split-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CelebA loaders
│   ├── methods/               # Fisher, gradient ascent, SISA
│   ├── signals/               # MIA, oracle gap, activation, attribution, loss landscape
│   ├── models/                # Small CNN / MLP backbones
│   └── utils/                 # Seeding, metrics, logging
├── configs/                   # YAML experiment configs (per dataset)
├── experiments/               # Shell scripts for batch runs
├── results/                   # Output tables and figures (gitignored for large files)
├── tests/                     # Unit + integration tests
├── paper/                     # LaTeX proposal writeup and final report
├── docs/
│   ├── proposal/              # Submitted proposal deck
│   └── study_notes/           # Team technical reference docs
├── run_benchmark.py           # Unified benchmark entrypoint
├── pyproject.toml             # Build system + tool configuration
└── requirements.txt           # Pinned dependencies
```

---

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/soumikbhatta/unlearnbench.git
cd unlearnbench

python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Run the first benchmark: gradient ascent on Split-MNIST, verify with MIA + Oracle Gap
python run_benchmark.py \
  --dataset split_mnist \
  --method gradient_ascent \
  --signals mia oracle_gap \
  --seed 42
```

---

## Current Status

**Stage:** Proposal complete — implementation scaffold in progress.

| Component                               | Status        |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Project framing & proposal deck         | ✅ Complete    |
| Repository structure                    | ✅ Complete    |
| Dataset loaders (Split-MNIST, CIFAR-10) | 🔧 In progress |
| Base training pipeline + checkpointing  | 🔧 In progress |
| Gradient Ascent unlearning              | 🔧 In progress |
| Fisher Forgetting                       | 🔧 In progress |
| MIA verification signal                 | 🔧 In progress |
| Oracle Gap signal                       | 🔧 In progress |
| SISA training                           | 📅 Planned     |
| Activation analysis                     | 📅 Planned     |
| Feature attribution (GradCAM)           | 📅 Planned     |
| Loss landscape (Hessian)                | 📅 Stretch     |
| CelebA support                          | 📅 Stretch     |
| Unified results table                   | 📅 Planned     |
| Final report (NeurIPS format)           | 📅 Due May 6   |

---

## Team

| Name                       | Email                      | Role                                         |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| **Soumik Bhatta**          | soumikbhatta@umass.edu     | Orchestration, benchmark framing, Oracle Gap |
| **Sagnik Chatterjee**      | sagnikchatterjee@umass.edu | Dataset loaders, training pipeline           |
| **B Vishnu Vardhan Reddy** | bvishnuvardhanr@umass.edu  | Unlearning methods, metrics, results         |

---

## Key References

- Golatkar, A. et al. (2020). *Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Net: Selective Forgetting in Deep Networks.* NeurIPS.
- Bourtoule, L. et al. (2021). *Machine Unlearning.* IEEE S&P.
- Carlini, N. et al. (2022). *Membership Inference Attacks From First Principles.* IEEE S&P.

---

## Deadlines

| Deliverable                        | Due               |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| ~~Proposal slides~~                | ~~Mar 1~~ ✅       |
| Proposal presentation              | **Mar 2** ← today |
| Proposal writeup (1 page, NeurIPS) | Mar 9             |
| Partial results video (3–5 min)    | Mar 30            |
| Final presentation (5–10 min)      | Apr 27 / May 4    |
| Final report (5–9 pages, NeurIPS)  | May 6             |

---

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

    19→a model can fool MIA while retaining structural traces of the "forgotten" data in its
    20→weights, activations, and loss landscape.
    21→
    22→**Our contribution:** run 3 unlearning baselines through 5 verification signals and compare
    23→them against an oracle (model retrained from scratch). We call the gap between an unlearned
    24→model and the oracle the **Oracle Gap**.
    25→

    27→

    67→
    68→## Core concepts (know these before writing code)
    69→
    70→### Oracle Gap
    71→The distance between an **unlearned model** and a model **retrained from scratch** on the retain set only.
    72→The retrained model is the gold standard — it never saw the forget set.
    73→```
    74→Oracle Gap = some_metric(unlearned_model, oracle_model)
    75→```
    76→Implemented metrics: L2 parameter distance, cosine similarity.
    77→Perfect unlearning = Oracle Gap of 0 across all signals.
    78→
    79→### Forget set / Retain set
    80→The training data is split into:
    81→- **Forget set (F):** data points the model should "unlearn"
    82→- **Retain set (R):** everything else — model keeps this knowledge
    83→
    84→In Split-MNIST, each "task" is a pair of digit classes. Forget set = one full task (e.g. digits 0+1).
    85→
    86→### The 3 unlearning methods
    87→
    88→**1. Gradient Ascent** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/gradient_ascent.py`)
    89→- Maximize (instead of minimize) cross-entropy loss on the forget set
    90→- Fast, simple. Risk: destabilizes retain performance if too aggressive
    91→
    92→**2. Fisher Forgetting** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/fisher.py`)
    93→- Measure which weights are important for the retain set (Fisher Information diagonal)
    94→- Add noise inversely proportional to Fisher importance
    95→- Based on: Golatkar et al. NeurIPS 2020
    96→
    97→**3. SISA Training** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/sisa.py` — not yet implemented)
    98→- Shard the training data. Train on each shard separately. To unlearn, only retrain the affected shard.
    99→- Exact unlearning (provably correct). More expensive upfront.
   100→- Based on: Bourtoule et al. IEEE S&P 2021
   101→
   102→### The 5 verification signals
   103→
   104→**Tier 1 (implement first):**
   105→- `signals/mia.py` — Membership Inference Attack: can an adversary tell if a sample was in training? AUC ~0.5 = looks unlearned.
   106→- `signals/oracle_gap.py` — L2/cosine distance between unlearned model and oracle model parameters.
   107→
   108→**Tier 2 (implement after Tier 1 works):**
   109→- `signals/activation_analysis.py` — do hidden layers still respond to forget-set data? (not yet started)
   110→- `signals/feature_attribution.py` — GradCAM saliency on forget-set images (not yet started)
   111→

# AGENTS.md — UnlearnBench AI Context File

> **Step 1: Read [RULES.md](./RULES.md) before anything else.**
> RULES.md defines the source of truth hierarchy, anti-hallucination rules,
> file ownership, and implementation order. It overrides everything else.
> **Step 2: Read this file for project context and current status.**

---

## What is this project?

**UnlearnBench** is a CS 590NN course project at UMass Amherst (Spring 2026).

The project builds a benchmark to evaluate machine unlearning methods.

**Machine unlearning:** removing the influence of specific training data from a model,
required by GDPR "right to be forgotten." The standard way to verify that unlearning
worked is a Membership Inference Attack (MIA). We argue MIA alone is insufficient —
a model can fool MIA while retaining structural traces of the "forgotten" data in its
weights, activations, and loss landscape.

**Our contribution:** run 3 unlearning baselines through 5 verification signals and compare
them against an oracle (model retrained from scratch). We call the gap between an unlearned
model and the oracle the **Oracle Gap**.

---

## Team and AI agent roles

| Person                           | GitHub           | Their AI setup            | Their job                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Soumik Bhatta** (orchestrator) | @soumikbhatta    | Antigravity + Claude Code | Repo structure, Oracle Gap signal, integration, final report      |
| **Sagnik Chatterjee**            | @sagnikc395      | Cursor / Claude           | Dataset loaders, base training pipeline, checkpointing            |
| **Vishnu Vardhan Reddy**         | @VishnuVardhanBR | Cursor / Claude           | Unlearning methods (Fisher, GA, SISA), MIA signal, results tables |

**If you are Sagnik's AI:** focus on `src/unlearnbench/datasets/` and `src/unlearnbench/utils/metrics.py`

**If you are Vishnu's AI:** focus on `src/unlearnbench/methods/` and `src/unlearnbench/signals/mia.py`

**If you are Soumik's AI:** focus on `src/unlearnbench/signals/oracle_gap.py`, `run_benchmark.py`, and integration

---

## Project status (as of March 2, 2026)

| Component                         | Status                           | Owner  |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------ |
| Proposal slides                   | ✅ Submitted                      | All    |
| Proposal presentation             | ⏰ Today 4PM in class             | All    |
| Proposal writeup (1 page NeurIPS) | 🔧 Not started — **due Mar 9**    | All    |

| run_benchmark.py                  | 🔧 Scaffold exists                | Soumik |
| Results table                     | ❌ Not started                    | All    |

---

## Core concepts (know these before writing code)

### Oracle Gap
The distance between an **unlearned model** and a model **retrained from scratch** on the retain set only.
The retrained model is the gold standard — it never saw the forget set.
```
Oracle Gap = some_metric(unlearned_model, oracle_model)
```
Implemented metrics: L2 parameter distance, cosine similarity.
Perfect unlearning = Oracle Gap of 0 across all signals.

### Forget set / Retain set
The training data is split into:
- **Forget set (F):** data points the model should "unlearn"
- **Retain set (R):** everything else — model keeps this knowledge

In Split-MNIST, each "task" is a pair of digit classes. Forget set = one full task (e.g. digits 0+1).

### The 3 unlearning methods

**1. Gradient Ascent** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/gradient_ascent.py`)
- Maximize (instead of minimize) cross-entropy loss on the forget set
- Fast, simple. Risk: destabilizes retain performance if too aggressive

**2. Fisher Forgetting** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/fisher.py`)
- Measure which weights are important for the retain set (Fisher Information diagonal)
- Add noise inversely proportional to Fisher importance
- Based on: Golatkar et al. NeurIPS 2020

**3. SISA Training** (`src/unlearnbench/methods/sisa.py` — not yet implemented)
- Shard the training data. Train on each shard separately. To unlearn, only retrain the affected shard.
- Exact unlearning (provably correct). More expensive upfront.
- Based on: Bourtoule et al. IEEE S&P 2021

### The 5 verification signals

**Tier 1 (implement first):**
- `signals/mia.py` — Membership Inference Attack: can an adversary tell if a sample was in training? AUC ~0.5 = looks unlearned.
- `signals/oracle_gap.py` — L2/cosine distance between unlearned model and oracle model parameters.

**Tier 2 (implement after Tier 1 works):**
- `signals/activation_analysis.py` — do hidden layers still respond to forget-set data? (not yet started)
- `signals/feature_attribution.py` — GradCAM saliency on forget-set images (not yet started)

**Tier 3 (stretch):**
- `signals/loss_landscape.py` — Hessian eigenspectrum analysis (not yet started)

---

## Repo structure

```

├── AGENTS.md                      ← YOU ARE HERE. Read this first.
├── README.md                      ← Public-facing project description
├── CONTRIBUTING.md                ← Branch naming, PR rules, responsibilities

├── configs/

│   └── cifar10.yaml               ← Experiment config for CIFAR-10
├── src/unlearnbench/
│   ├── datasets/

│   │   └── cifar10.py             ← Split-CIFAR-10 loaders
│   ├── methods/

│   │   ├── fisher.py              ← ✅ Scaffold done
│   │   └── sisa.py                ← ❌ Not implemented yet
│   ├── signals/
│   │   ├── mia.py                 ← ✅ Scaffold done
│   │   ├── oracle_gap.py          ← ✅ Scaffold done
│   │   ├── activation_analysis.py ← ❌ Not implemented yet
│   │   ├── feature_attribution.py ← ❌ Not implemented yet
│   │   └── loss_landscape.py      ← ❌ Not implemented yet (stretch)
│   ├── models/
│   │   └── simple_cnn.py          ← Small CNN for MNIST + CIFAR-10
│   └── utils/
│       ├── metrics.py             ← train(), evaluate() loops
│       └── seed.py                ← set_seed() for reproducibility
├── experiments/                   ← Shell scripts for batch runs
├── results/                       ← JSON outputs from run_benchmark.py
├── paper/                         ← LaTeX writeup (proposal_writeup.tex due Mar 9)
├── docs/
│   ├── proposal/                  ← Submitted proposal deck (PPTX + PDF)
│   └── study_notes/
│       └── team_bootstrap.md      ← Longer technical reference
└── tests/
    ├── unit/                      ← Unit tests (pytest)
    └── integration/               ← Integration tests
```

---

## How to run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/soumikbhatta/unlearnbench.git
cd unlearnbench
python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Quickest smoke test: gradient ascent on Split-MNIST, MIA + Oracle Gap
python run_benchmark.py \
  --dataset split_mnist \
  --method gradient_ascent \
  --signals mia oracle_gap \
  --epochs 5 \
  --seed 42
```

Results are saved as JSON to `results/`.

---

## Coding rules (enforced by CI)

- **Python 3.10+** only. Type hints on all public functions.
- **Linter:** `ruff check src/` — run before every commit.
- **Formatter:** `ruff format src/` — run before every commit.
- **No sklearn** in core signals (keeps dep tree light). MIA AUC is hand-computed.
- **No print statements** — use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`.
- **Every unlearning method** must have the same API:
  ```python
  def unlearn(self, model, forget_loader, retain_loader) -> nn.Module
  ```
- **Every signal** must have:
  ```python
  def compute(self, ...) -> dataclass_result
  ```

---

## Branch naming

```
soumik/feature-name
sagnik/feature-name
vishnu/feature-name
```

Never push directly to `main`. Open a PR, Soumik reviews and merges.

---

## Key paper references

| Method            | Paper                           | Key fact                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Fisher Forgetting | Golatkar et al., NeurIPS 2020   | Uses Fisher Information Matrix diagonal as importance weight |
| SISA              | Bourtoule et al., IEEE S&P 2021 | Sharded training enables exact, provable unlearning          |
| MIA baseline      | Carlini et al., IEEE S&P 2022   | Loss threshold attack; no shadow model needed                |
| Bio connection    | Nader et al., Science 2000      | Memory reconsolidation — retrieved memories become labile    |

Here's the full context of the project:

---

## UnlearnBench — Project Overview

**Course:** CS 590NN/690NN — Neural Networks in AI and Neuroscience, UMass Amherst (Spring 2026)
**Team:** Soumik Bhatta, Sagnik Chatterjee (you), B Vishnu Vardhan Reddy

---

### The Problem

**Machine unlearning** = removing the influence of specific training data from a model *without* full retraining. This is increasingly required by regulations like GDPR's "right to be forgotten."

The standard verification approach is a **Membership Inference Attack (MIA)** — testing whether an adversary can tell if a data point was in the training set. **The flaw:** a model can fool MIA through confidence calibration while still retaining structural traces of "forgotten" data in its weights, activations, and loss landscape.

---

### The Contribution

**UnlearnBench** proposes a multi-signal verification benchmark:

| Signal | What it measures | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| MIA | Can an adversary identify forgotten samples? | 1 |
| Oracle Gap (Weight Distance) | L2/cosine distance to retrained-from-scratch model | 1 |
| Activation Analysis | Hidden layer responses to forgotten data | 2 |
| Feature Attribution (GradCAM) | Where the model "looks" on forgotten samples | 2 |
| Loss Landscape (Hessian) | Second-order memory traces | Stretch |

These are applied across **3 unlearning baselines** (Fisher Forgetting, Gradient Ascent, SISA) on **Split-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CelebA**.

The key concept is the **Oracle Gap** — the measurable delta between an unlearned model and a model retrained from scratch (the gold standard). Perfect unlearning = Oracle Gap of zero across all signals.

---

### Your Role (Sagnik)

Focus on:
- `src/unlearnbench/datasets/` — Split-MNIST, CIFAR-10 loaders
- `src/unlearnbench/utils/metrics.py` — training/eval loops
- Base training pipeline and checkpointing

---

### Current Status

The repo has scaffolding in place for most Tier 1 components; many are marked "needs testing." SISA, activation analysis, feature attribution, and loss landscape are not yet started.
